bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

Whether you are negotiating a salary or checking your current earnings, converting an hourly rate to an annual figure is straightforward. The standard formula is:

**Annual gross pay ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

This article assumes a full-time working week of 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman for the National Employment Standards. If you work a different number of hours, adjust the calculation accordingly. The result is your gross annual income before tax, Medicare levy, and any salary packaging arrangements.

### Why 38 Hours and 52 Weeks?

The 38-hour week is the benchmark for full-time employment in Australia. Multiplying by 52 weeks gives a yearly total, but note that this assumes you work every week of the year with no unpaid leave. If you take annual leave or public holidays, your actual paid weeks may be fewer, but the formula remains a useful starting point. For a fortnightly comparison, simply double your weekly pay: hourly rate × 38 × 2.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. From 1 July 2026, the rate is **$26.44 per hour** for a permanent employee, equating to $1004.90 per week or $52,254.80 per year (before tax and super). Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate, making their minimum $33.05 per hour. This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave entitlements.

However, the National Minimum Wage is a safety net. Most employees are covered by an **award** – a legal document that sets minimum pay and conditions for a specific industry or occupation. Award rates are often higher than the national minimum. For example, a retail employee may have a higher base rate under the General Retail Industry Award. Always check the relevant award via the Fair Work Ombudsman’s website to ensure you are being paid correctly. Our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page provides more detail on current rates.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

If you are a casual employee, remember that the 25% loading is added to the base hourly rate **before** calculating annual pay. Do not enter a rate that already includes the loading – our [timesheet](/) allows you to tick a checkbox to apply the loading automatically.

Superannuation Guarantee contributions are paid **on top** of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a full-time employee on the National Minimum Wage, that means an extra $6,270.58 in super annually (12% of $52,254.80). Super is not included in your take-home pay; it goes into your nominated super fund. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Once you have your annual gross figure, you can estimate your tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for low-income earners). Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator uses these rates, but note that it does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

### Salary Sacrifice EV Australia

If you are considering a novated lease or salary packaging arrangement for an electric vehicle, you may be able to reduce your taxable income through **salary sacrifice EV Australia**. This involves your employer diverting part of your pre-tax salary to cover the cost of the vehicle and its running expenses. While this can lower your tax bill, it also reduces your ordinary earnings for superannuation purposes (unless you salary sacrifice into super separately). Our estimates do not include salary sacrifice arrangements – they assume your full hourly rate is ordinary earnings. For personalised advice, speak to a tax professional or your employer. The [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page has more on how packaging affects your pay.

### Using the Hourly to Annual Converter

Our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate and see the annual, fortnightly, and weekly equivalents. If you are a casual, tick the casual loading box to add 25% automatically. The result shows gross pay, estimated tax, Medicare, and super. Remember that this is an estimate only – actual pay may vary due to penalties, allowances, or salary sacrifice.

### Fortnightly Pay in Context

Many employers pay fortnightly. To get your fortnightly gross, multiply your weekly pay by two. For example, on the National Minimum Wage: $1004.90 × 2 = $2009.80 per fortnight. After tax and Medicare, your take-home will be lower, but super is paid on top and not deducted from your pocket.

### Average Earnings vs Your Rate

The Australian Bureau of Statistics publishes Average Weekly Earnings. In May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings were **$2083.70 per week** (about $108,352 per year). All employees total earnings (including part-time) averaged **$1579.20 per week**. These are averages, not medians, and they vary by industry and state. Our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page provides more context, but remember that your own rate depends on your award, agreement, or individual contract.

### Final Thoughts

Converting your hourly rate to annual pay is a simple calculation, but understanding the components – minimum wage, award rates, casual loading, super, and tax – gives you a clearer picture of your total remuneration. If you are exploring salary sacrifice EV Australia, factor that into your budget separately. Always refer to official sources such as the Fair Work Ombudsman and the Australian Taxation Office for the most accurate and up-to-date information.
